lede: Quiet news day dominated by test-flakiness tooling and a new round of agentic coding benchmarks. Nothing structural, but two releases worth a closer look if you run large E2E suites.

items.title: Playwright 1.48 ships built-in flaky-test quarantine
items.summary: Failing tests can now be auto-tagged and re-run in isolation instead of blocking the whole suite, with a report diffing quarantine hits over time.

items.title: New benchmark measures agentic coding tools on real bug reports, not katas
items.summary: Researchers replaced synthetic coding puzzles with 400 real GitHub issues, and ranking shifts noticeably once the tasks stop being toy problems.

items.title: Google publishes internal 'test impact analysis' post-mortem
items.summary: A retrospective on why selective test execution rolled out three times before it stuck, with concrete false-negative numbers from each attempt.

items.title: k6 adds native browser-based Core Web Vitals checks
items.summary: Load tests can now assert on LCP and INP alongside throughput, closing a long-standing gap between performance and UX testing.

items.title: Survey: 61% of QA teams now maintain an internal LLM eval suite
items.summary: The State of QA 2026 survey shows eval-writing overtaking manual exploratory testing as a stated primary duty for the first time.

items.title: GitHub Actions adds per-job carbon estimate in run summaries
items.summary: CI runs now surface an estimated CO2e figure next to duration and cost, sourced from runner region and instance type.
